topic: What is Logistics Management? - Camcode · Part 3/4

passage.text: Reverse logistics focuses on return processes when end consumers receive products that do not meet their requirements or were damaged during delivery. It deals with the transportation and storage of finished goods, rather than raw materials. In standard logistics, goods move from a seller, manufacturer, or storage facility to an end consumer. In reverse logistics, the direction is opposite: finished goods move from the end consumer back to the seller or manufacturer. Reverse logistics may also include processes such as inspecting returned items, refurbishing them, and redistributing them. It may also cover the disposal of items that cannot be repaired or resold.
